It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was alone with Mariyah on the day of ʿĀʾishah, and Ḥafṣah learned of this. So he said to her: "Keep this secret for me, and I have made Mariyah forbidden to myself. This is because forbidding what Allah has made lawful has two aspects. The first: believing that the ruling of prohibition applies to it. This is equivalent to believing the ruling of permissibility for what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden, and both are prohibited and do not come from those who bear the mark of faith. If it does come from them, the believer loses the ruling and the name of faith. The second: abstaining from what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made lawful. Describing it as prohibition by its mere wording is correct, as in His words ﴿And We had forbidden him the wet-nurses before﴾ [28:12], meaning: We prevented, nothing more. If forbidding were treating the permissible as prohibited, and abstaining from it were impermissible, the reality of the matter would be impossible to resolve without difficulty. Even ordinary believers are too exalted to hold that what Allah has made lawful for them is forbidden, so how could he not hold the station of the Prophet (peace be upon him) too high for what the station of the common nation is elevated above? This statement by al-Zamakhshari is nothing but audacity against Allah and His Messenger, and speaking without verification, and presenting a corrupt opinion without refinement. We seek refuge in Allah from that. He is the One asked to make our means to Him the glorification of our Prophet, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, to keep us away from the steps of Satan, and to forgive us for the slips of the tongue. Āmīn.]], and I give you good news that Abu Bakr and ʿUmar will rule my community after me." So ʿĀʾishah was informed of it, and they were close friends. Ḥafṣah went to ʿĀʾishah and informed her, so Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ [66:1], and he was commanded to expiate his oath and he restrained his wives." If you say: What is the ruling on forbidding what is lawful? I say: This has been disputed. Abū Ḥanīfah regards it as an oath in every case, and considers the intended benefit in what one forbids. So if he forbids food, he has sworn not to eat it; or a slave-girl, then not to have intercourse with her; or a wife, then it is an īlāʾ (oath of abstention) from her, if he has no intention. If he intends ẓihār, it is ẓihār; if he intends divorce, it is irrevocable divorce, "and likewise if he intends two; if he intends three, then as he intended; and if he says, 'I intended to lie,' he is believed between himself and Allah, but he is not believed in court to annul the īlāʾ." If he says, "Everything lawful is forbidden to me," then it applies to food and drink if he has no intention, otherwise to what he intended. Al-Shāfiʿī does not regard it as an oath, but as a cause for expiation regarding women only. If he intends divorce, it is revocable according to him. It is reported from Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd and Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them) that "the forbidden is an oath" [[The ḥadīth of Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was narrated by Ibn Abī Shaybah through Juwaybir from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, that Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd said: Whoever says to his wife, "You are forbidden to me," she is not forbidden, and he owes the expiation of an oath. Its chain is weak and disconnected. The ḥadīth of ʿUmar is similar, and has another route narrated by Ibn Abī Shaybah from the narration of Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ from ʿIkrimah, from him, who said: "The forbidden is an oath." This is disconnected. The ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) is similar and agreed upon, through Ibn Jubayr from him, who said: "The forbidden is an oath, for which one makes expiation." In a narration of Muslim: "When a man forbids his wife, it is an oath which he expiates." The ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd is similar, and has another route narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzāq from al-Ṭabarānī, from Ibn ʿUqbah, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from him, who said: "Regarding the forbidden, it is an oath which one expiates." Its narrators are trustworthy despite its disconnection. The ḥadīth of Zayd ibn Thābit (may Allah be pleased with him) is similar.]]. From ʿUmar: if he intends divorce, it is revocable. From ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him): three. From Zayd: one irrevocable. From ʿUthmān: ẓihār [[Ibn Abī Shaybah and ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated from the narration of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAlī, regarding a man's saying to his wife, "You are forbidden to me": "She is three." This is also disconnected.]].

Masrūq used to regard it as nothing, and said: "I do not care whether you forbid her or a bowl of thārīd." Similarly, al-Shaʿbī said: "It is nothing," citing His words ﴿And do not say, about what your tongues describe falsely: "This is lawful and this is unlawful"﴾ [16:116], and His words ﴿Do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [5:87]. Whatever Allah has not forbidden, no one has the right to forbid it, nor to make it forbidden by forbidding it. It is not established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said of what Allah had made lawful, "It is forbidden to me." He refrained from Mariyah only because of an oath he had made earlier, which was his saying (peace be upon him): "By Allah, I will not approach her after today." So it was said to him: ﴿Why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ [66:1], meaning: you did not refrain from it because of the oath. That is, proceed with what you swore to, and make expiation for your oath. Similar to it is His words ﴿And We had forbidden him the wet-nurses﴾ [28:12], meaning: We prevented him from them. The apparent meaning of His words ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ is that he had indeed made an oath.

If you say: Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) make expiation for that? I say: From al-Ḥasan: he did not make expiation, because he was forgiven what he had done before and what came after. [[I have not found it. In Abū Dāwūd's al-Marāsīl there is something different from this, which he narrated through Qatādah from him, regarding the forbidding of Umm Ibrahim. He said: "He was commanded to expiate his oath," and similarly Ibn Isḥāq mentioned it, as already stated, that he expiated his oath.]] Rather, it is only a teaching for the believers. From Muqātil: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) freed a slave in the matter of forbidding Mariyah. ﴿And Allah is your Mawlā﴾: your master and the one who manages your affairs. ﴿And He is the All-Knowing﴾ of what makes you righteous, so He legislates it for you. ﴿The All-Wise﴾, so He does not command you or forbid you except with what wisdom requires. It was said: "Your Mawlā is more entitled to you than yourselves, so His counsel is more beneficial to you than your own counsel to yourselves."

If you say: What is the ruling on forbidding what is lawful? I say: This has been disputed. Abū Ḥanīfah regards it as an oath in every case, and considers the intended benefit in what one forbids. From ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him): three. From Zayd: one irrevocable. From ʿUthmān: ẓihār [[Ibn Abī Shaybah and ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated from the narration of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAlī, regarding a man's saying to his wife, "You are forbidden to me": "She is three." **Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 66, verse 4:**

﴿If you two repent﴾: this is addressed to Hafsa and Aisha, in the style of *iltifat* (a shift in grammatical person), which makes the reproach more forceful.

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas: "I had been keen to ask Umar about the two of them until he performed the Hajj and I performed it with him. When we were on part of the road, he deviated and I deviated with him carrying the water-skin. I poured water over his hand and he performed ablution. I said: 'Who are the two?' He said: 'Wonder, Ibn Abbas!' as if he disliked what I had asked about. Then he said: 'They are Hafsa and Aisha.'" [[Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim).]]

﴿Your hearts have indeed swerved﴾: this means that something has occurred from you both that necessitates repentance, namely the inclination of your hearts away from what is obligatory in sincere devotion to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which is loving what he loves and disliking what he dislikes. Ibn Mas'ud recited: ﴿your hearts have deviated﴾.

﴿And if you two support one another against him﴾: that is, by cooperating against him through what would displease him, such as excessive jealousy and disclosing his secret. ﴿Then indeed Allah is his protector﴾, that is, his guardian and helper. He will not lack one who supports him. And how could one who supports him against Allah, his Lord, be [counted]? The addition ﴿He﴾ is a declaration that his support is one of his resolute acts, and that he undertakes it personally.

﴿And Gabriel﴾: he is the head of the *kurubiyyun* (the cherubim). His mention is coupled with the mention of Allah and singled out from among the angels, to honour him and to show his high station with Him.

﴿And the righteous among the believers﴾: that is, whoever among the believers is righteous, meaning everyone who believes and does righteous deeds. It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "those who are free of hypocrisy among them." It has also been said: the prophets. It has been said: the Companions. It has been said: the caliphs among them.

If you ask: is *salih al-mu'minin* (the righteous of the believers) singular or plural? I answer: it is singular, used to mean the plural, like your saying: "This righteous one among people does not do this," meaning the category, as your saying: "Whoever among them is righteous does not do it." Similarly your saying: "I was in the evening gathering and the daytime gathering." It is also permissible that its original form was *salihu al-mu'minin* with a waw, written without the waw according to the pronunciation, because the wording is the same for singular and plural in it, as some things have come in the Mushaf where the rule of pronunciation is followed rather than the form of the script.

﴿And the angels﴾: despite their multitude and the filling of the heavens with their hosts. ﴿After that﴾: after the support of Allah, his confidant, and the righteous believers. ﴿Are a supporting company﴾: a group that backs him, as though they were one hand against whoever opposes him. How then could the support of two women against one whose supporters are these reach [any effect]?

If you ask: the phrase ﴿after that﴾ is an exaltation of the angels and their support, yet the support of Allah, Gabriel and the righteous believers has already been mentioned, and the support of Allah is greater and greater still. I answer: the support of the angels is part of the support of Allah. It is as though He preferred His support through them and their backing over the other aspects of His support, because of their superiority over all His creation.

[[Her words "because of their superiority over all His creation": the doctrine of the Mu'tazila (a rationalist theological school) is that angels are superior to humans, while the People of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna) hold that some humans are superior to angels. (Editor's note: "ʿ" marker.)]]

It is also read: ﴿you two support﴾, ﴿you two (both) support﴾, and ﴿you two help﴾.

Read (with and without the shadda, for the sake of plurality): yubaddilahu. Muslimat (submitting), mu'minat (believing), qanitat (obedient), ta'ibat (repentant), 'abidat (worshipping), sa'ihat (fasting); a reading is also reported as sayyihat, which is more emphatic. It was said that the fasting woman is called sa'ih (wanderer), because the wanderer has no provision with him, so he keeps holding back until he finds something to eat; thus the fasting person is likened to him in holding back until the time of his breaking the fast comes. It was also said: sa'ihat means emigrating (muhajirat). From Zayd ibn Aslam: there was no siyahah (wandering) in this community except hijrah (emigration).

If you say: how can the substituted wives be better than them, when there were no women on the face of the earth better than the Mothers of the Believers? [[His words "women better than the Mothers of the Believers" is perhaps "better" (khayran). (ed.)]] I say: if the Messenger of God divorces them for their disobedience to him and their harming him, they will no longer retain that quality, and others who are described with these attributes, together with obedience to the Messenger of God ﷺ and submission to his desire and pleasure, would be better than them. This is alluded to in His words ﴿qanitat﴾, because qunut is standing in obedience to God, and obedience to God lies in obedience to His Messenger.

I say: because they are two contrasting attributes which cannot be combined in the way the rest of the attributes can be combined, so there was no escape from the waw.

It is recited as wa-qūduhā with a ḍamma, meaning "its fuel-possessor." If you say: are not the two clauses of one meaning? I say: No; the meaning of the first is that they accept His commands and bind themselves to them, neither refusing nor denying them. The meaning of the second is that they carry out what they are commanded, neither slacking nor delaying in it. If you say: God addressed the polytheists who denied the revelation with this very thing in His saying: "But if you do not, and you will never do, then guard against the Fire whose fuel is people and stones," and said it was prepared for the disbelievers; so what is the meaning of addressing the believers with it? Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 66, verse 8:

"Sincere repentance" (﴿tawbatan nasuhan﴾). Repentance is described as sincere by way of metaphorical attribution (al-isnad al-majazi, a figure in which an attribute is ascribed to something other than its true subject). Sincerity (nush) is a quality of the repenters: they give sincere counsel to themselves regarding repentance, so they carry it out in its proper way, making up for shortcomings and erasing misdeeds. This means that they repent of ugly deeds because of their ugliness, regretting them, grieving intensely over having committed them, and resolving that they will not return to any ugly deed until the milk returns to the udder, preparing themselves for that.

It is reported from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard a Bedouin say: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance." He said: "O you, quickness of the tongue in repentance is the repentance of liars." The man asked: "And what is repentance?" He said: "It comprises six things: for past sins, regret; for the obligatory duties you neglected, making them up; restoring what was taken unjustly; seeking the pardon of those you wronged; resolving never to return to it; and melting your soul in obedience to Allah just as you had nurtured it in disobedience, and making it taste the bitterness of obedience just as you made it taste the sweetness of sins."

From Hudhayfah: "It is enough of evil for a man that he repents of a sin and then returns to it." From Shahr ibn Hawshab: "(Sincere repentance is) that he does not return to it even if he is cut with a sword and burned with fire." From Ibn al-Sammak: "(It is) that you place before your eyes the sin in which you showed little shame before Allah, and prepare yourself for what awaits you." It was also said: "(It is) a repentance that one never has to repent of again." From al-Suddi: "Repentance is not valid unless it involves giving sincere counsel to oneself and to the believers, for whoever's repentance is sound loves that people be like him."

It was also said: "Nasuhan" derives from nasahat al-thawb (mending a garment), meaning: a repentance that mends your tears in your religion and patches your rents. [[The author's words "and patches your rents" (wa tarimmu khallaka): in the Sihah, "al-khall" is a worn-out garment; the wording of al-Nasafi is "khallaka." In the Sihah, "al-khalal" (with a vowel on the kh) is a gap between two things, and corruption in a matter. (Editor's note)]] It was also said: "(It means) pure," from the expression "honey nasih," meaning honey that has been cleared of wax. It may also be understood as: a repentance that gives counsel to people, that is, that calls them to the like of it, because its effect is evident in the one who performs it, and in his diligence and resolve in carrying out its requirements.

Zayd ibn Ali read "tawban nasuhan" (with the accusative). It is also read "nushan" (with a ḍamma), which is a verbal noun of nasaha. Nasah and nasuh are like shukr and shakur, and kufr and kafur, meaning: possessing sincerity, or: let it be sincere, or: repent for the sake of your own sincerity, with it as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu).

﴿It may be that your Lord will remove your misdeeds from you﴾ (ʿasā rabbukum): This is an expression of hope from Allah to His servants, and it has two aspects. The first is that it follows the habit of kings in using "ʿasā" and "laʿalla," and in such usage it is taken as a firm and definite matter. The second is that it comes to teach the servants that they must balance between fear and hope. What indicates the first meaning, that it is in the sense of a definite decision, is the reading of Ibn Abi ʿAbla: "wa-yudkhilakum" (with the jussive), which is coordinated with the position of "ʿasā rabbukum an yukaffira," as if it were said: "Repent, and that will make Him remove your misdeeds, and cause you to enter..."

﴿The day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet﴾ (yawma la yukhzi Allahu): "yawma" is in the accusative, governed by "yudkhilakum." "La yukhzi" is an indirect reproach to those whom Allah has disgraced among the people of unbelief and wickedness, and an expression of praise toward the believers, that He has protected them from a condition like theirs.

﴿Their light runs before them and on their right hands﴾ (yasʿā nūruhum ʿalā al-sirāt): ﴿Our Lord, perfect our light for us﴾ (atmim lanā nūranā). Ibn Abbas said: "They say this when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished, out of apprehension." It is also reported from al-Hasan: "Allah will complete it for them, but they supplicate in order to draw near to Allah, as in His saying: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾, although he is already forgiven." It was also said: it is said by the lowest-ranked of them, because they are given light only to the extent that they can see the place where their feet tread, since light is in proportion to deeds, so they ask for its completion as a favor.

It was also said: those who are foremost to Paradise pass over the bridge (al-sirat) like lightning, some like the wind, and some crawling and dragging themselves; and it is these who say: ﴿Our Lord, perfect our light for us﴾.

If you ask: how can they feel apprehension when the believers are secure? ﴿Is he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection [like the one who does not]?﴾ and ﴿There shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve, [for the greatest terror will not grieve them]﴾. Or how can they seek nearness when the abode is not an abode of seeking nearness? I say: as for apprehension, it may be a matter of human nature, even though they believe themselves secure. As for seeking nearness, since their condition is like the condition of those who seek nearness, in that they ask for what is already theirs of mercy, it is called seeking nearness.

Strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and against the hypocrites with argument, and show harshness and severity toward both groups in whatever you strive against them with, whether fighting or disputation. It is reported from Qatadah: the striving against the hypocrites is to establish the prescribed punishments (hudud) upon them. It is reported from Mujahid: it is with threat. And it has been said: it is by exposing their secrets.

God, may He be exalted, presented the example of the state of the disbelievers, in that they are punished for their disbelief and their enmity toward the believers with a punishment like theirs [[His words "the state of the disbelievers, in that they are punished for their disbelief" refer to those who have a relationship with the believers. And his words "like theirs" refer to those who have no relationship with the believers. (ع)]], without leniency or favoritism. Their enmity toward the believers does not benefit them, nor does the blood tie of kinship or the bond of marriage that existed between them. Their enmity toward the believers and their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger sever all ties and cut off connections, making them more distant than strangers, and even more distant. Even if the believer to whom the disbeliever is connected is one of the prophets of Allah, the example is the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. When the two of them were hypocritical and betrayed the two Messengers, the two Messengers did not avail them at all against Allah's punishment, despite the bond of marriage between them. It was said to them, at their death or on the Day of Resurrection:

﴿Enter the Fire along with those who enter it﴾, that is, with the rest of those who enter, who have no bond with the prophets, or with those among your brethren from the people of Noah and the people of Lot who enter it.

And the example of the state of the believers, in that the connection of the disbelievers does not harm them or diminish anything of their reward and nearness to Allah, is the wife of Pharaoh and her station with Allah, Exalted is He, despite her being the wife of the greatest enemy of Allah, who proclaimed the supreme word. And Mary, daughter of Imran, and what she was granted of the honor of this world and the Hereafter, and her being chosen above the women of the worlds, even though her people were disbelievers. Within these two examples lies an allusion to the two mothers of the believers mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and what had transpired from them of backing each other against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [[His words "backing each other against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)" are perhaps "backing each other" (al-tazahur min), as in the wording of al-Nasafi. (ع)]] in what displeased him, and a warning to them in the strongest and most severe manner, because of the mention of disbelief in the example. A similar severity is found in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾. It also indicates that it is incumbent upon the two of them to be in sincerity and to be perfect in it, like these two believing women, and not to rely on the fact that they are wives of the Messenger of Allah, for that merit does not benefit them except when they are sincere. The allusion is more fitting to Hafsah, because the wife of Lot disclosed his secrets just as Hafsah disclosed the secret of the Messenger of Allah. The secrets and symbols of the Revelation in every chapter reach such a degree of subtlety and concealment that it is too fine for the scholar's perception and slips past his insight.

If you say: what is the benefit of His words "from Our servants"? I say: since the basis of the example rests on the existence of righteousness in a person, whoever he may be, and that it alone is what brings success and attains what is with Allah, He said "two of Our righteous servants," mentioning the two well-known prophets, who are described as servants and were no different from the rest of Our servants, with no distinction between them and others except by righteousness alone, for clarification and manifestation, because a servant among the servants is preferred in His sight only by righteousness and nothing else, and whatever else by which people are preferred among people is not a cause of preference in His sight. If you say: what was their betrayal? I say: their hypocrisy and concealment of disbelief, and their backing of the two Messengers. The wife of Noah said to her people, "He is a madman," and the wife of Lot informed on his guests. It is not permissible to take betrayal to mean fornication, because it is repugnant in natural disposition and a defect in the eyes of everyone, unlike disbelief, for disbelievers do not find it repugnant but rather consider it good and call it truth. And from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "No wife of a prophet ever committed adultery" [[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Tabari and Ibn Mardawayh through a chain from him in the tafsir of Hud and here.]].

Wa-imra'at Fir'awn (And the wife of Pharaoh): Asiya bint Muzahim. It is also said that she was the paternal aunt of Musa, peace be upon him. She believed when she heard of the swallowing of the falsehood by Musa's staff, and Pharaoh tortured her. It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that Pharaoh pegged his wife down with four stakes, faced her toward the sun, laid her on her back, and placed a millstone on her chest. It is also said that he ordered a great rock to be dropped upon her, so she called upon Allah, and her soul was raised up, and the rock fell upon a body with no soul in it.

It is narrated from al-Hasan: Allah rescued her with the most honourable rescue, and raised her to Paradise, where she eats, drinks and enjoys herself. It is also said that when she said, ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾, she was shown her house in Paradise being built. And it is said that it was of a pearl.

It is also said that she was tortured in the sun, and the angels would shade her. If you ask: what is the meaning of combining "with You" (ʿindaka) and "in Paradise" (fī l-Janna)? I say: she sought nearness to the mercy of Allah and distance from the punishment of His enemies. Then she specified the place of nearness by her words ﴿in Paradise﴾. Or she meant the elevation of rank in Paradise, and that her garden be one of the gardens nearest to the Throne, namely the Gardens of Refuge (Jannat al-Ma'wa). So she expressed nearness to the Throne by her words ﴿with You﴾.

﴿from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾: from the deeds of Pharaoh. Or from the wicked self of Pharaoh and his tyrannical rule, and especially from his deed, which is disbelief, the worship of idols, oppression, and torture without any crime. ﴿And deliver me from the wrongdoing people﴾: from all the Copts. In this is evidence that seeking refuge in Allah, turning to Him, and asking for deliverance from Him at times of trial and calamity is part of the way of the righteous and the practice of the prophets and messengers: ﴿So judge between us and them with a judgement, and deliver me and those of the believers who are with me﴾ [Q 26:118–119], ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, and deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people﴾ [Q 10:85–86].

﴿in her**[[fīhi]]**﴾: in her private part (al-farj). Ibn Mas'ud read fīhā, as it was read in Surat al-Anbiya', the pronoun referring to the clause; and I have previously made remarks on this adverbial construction. Among the strange interpretations is that al-farj means the collar of the shirt, and that the meaning of "I guarded her" is that she prevented Jibril (from her). And it is also said that the verse combined in the example one who has a husband and one who has no husband, as consolation for widows and to comfort their hearts.

﴿and she affirmed the words of her Lord and His books﴾: it is read with both the shadda and without it, on the basis that she made the words and the books truthful, meaning she described them as true, and this is the very meaning of affirming (taṣdīq). If you ask: what are the words of Allah and His books? I say: it is permissible that by His words is meant the scrolls which He sent down to Idris and others. He called them "words" because of their brevity [[Mahmud said: "It is permissible that by the 'words' is meant the scrolls which Allah sent down to Idris and others; He called them 'words' because of their brevity..." etc. Ahmad said: he holds that the speech of Allah is created and denies the eternal speech. Therefore his speech does not go beyond indicating that the words of Allah are finite, for in the first aspect he made them a plural of paucity because of their brevity, and in the second he restricted them by his saying "all". And how far is his description of them as brief and restricted from the two twin verses, one of which is His saying: "Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord..." [Q 18:109], and the other His saying: "And if all the trees on the earth were pens..." [Q 31:27], the verse. He is in reality none other than one who does not believe in the words of Allah. The truth is that the speech of Allah is one of His attributes of perfection, eternal and everlasting, not finite. Thus did the wife of Pharaoh believe, whose praise is recited in the Book of the Mighty Allah. May Allah keep us firm in faith and protect us from abandonment, and Allah is the One sought for help.]], and His books: the four books [[His saying "and His books: the four books" — perhaps she knew of the Gospel and the Qur'an being sent down.]], and it may mean all that Allah spoke to His angels and others, and all that He wrote in the Preserved Tablet and elsewhere. It is also read as "the word of Allah and His scripture", meaning: by Jesus and by the scripture sent down to him, which is the Gospel. If you ask: why is it said ﴿of the devout﴾ in the masculine? I say: because devotion (qunut) is a description that includes whoever is devout from both sexes, so its masculine form predominates over its feminine. And ﴿min﴾ is partitive. It may also be for the starting point, on the basis that she was born of the devout, for she was among the descendants of Harun, brother of Musa, may the blessings of Allah be upon them both.

It is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: "Many men have attained perfection, but none of the women have attained perfection except four: Asiya bint Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh; Maryam bint Imran; Khadija bint Khuwaylid; and Fatima bint Muhammad. And the excellence of 'A'isha over the women is like the excellence of tharid over all other food." [[Recorded by al-Tha'labi through the chain of ʿAmr ibn Marzuq from Shuʿba from ʿAmr ibn Murra, who heard Murra from Abu Musa with this wording. Abu Nu'aym also recorded it in al-Hilya in the biography of ʿAmr ibn Murra by this route: "Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Yusuf al-Qadi narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Marzuq narrated to us with this." It is in al-Bukhari through Murra from Abu Musa without mention of Khadija and Fatima, may Allah be pleased with them. In Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim, from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, raised to the Prophet: "The best women of the worlds are four..." and he mentioned it.]] As for what is narrated that 'A'isha asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ how Allah named the believing woman, meaning Maryam, and did not name the disbelieving woman, he said: "Her name?" She said: "And what is her name?" He said: "The name of Noah's wife was 'Wali'a' and the name of Lot's wife was 'Wahila'." The fabrication in this report is clearly evident. Allah has named a group of disbelievers by their names and their kunyas. Had naming been an expression of love and its omission an expression of hatred, He would have named Asiya. Yet He has linked her with Maryam in the parable for the believers, and Allah refuses except to place in what is fabricated a sign that exposes it. The words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are wiser and safer than that.

It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Whoever recites Surat al-Tahrim, Allah will grant him sincere repentance (tawba nasuha)." [[Recorded by al-Tha'labi and Ibn Mardawayh with their chains to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]]
